docs.text: GDScript: api.reloading := false (property) True while the mod's setup re-runs for a quick reload (see engine/server/mod_reload.gd): blocks, items and entities that exist update in place; things that cannot change live are skipped and noted.
docs.title: api.reloading

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_ambience(options: Dictionary) -> String JavaScript: api.registerAmbience(options: { sound: string; every?: [number, number]; sky?: boolean; depth?: [number, number]; biome?: string | string[]; near?: string | string[]; radius?: number; chance?: number; volume?: number; pitch?: number; }): string Registers an occasional atmospheric sound near a player: wind out in the open, a drip in the dark, water lapping by a lake. Returns "" or why it was refused. api.register_ambience({"sound": "wind", "sky": true, "every": [20.0, 45.0]}) api.register_ambience({"sound": "drip", "sky": false, "depth": [0, 45], "every": [8.0, 25.0]}) api.register_ambience({"sound": "lapping", "near": ["base:water"], "radius": 6}) Conditions: sky (true outdoors, false under something), depth [low, high], biome (one or a list), near (block names - the sound then comes from one of them, so water laps from the water), radius , chance . every is [minimum, maximum] seconds, kept per player, so two people in different places hear their own surroundings rather than each other's. In the engine rather than in a mod because otherwise every mod that wanted weather or caves would write the same four decisions - how often is too often, how far can it be, who else hears it, what about somebody asleep - and none of them would agree. api.register_ambience({"sound": "proving:chime", "sky": true, "every": [20.0, 45.0]}) See also: register , set_default_role
docs.title: api.register_ambience

docs.text: GDScript: api.set_default_role(role_name: String) -> String JavaScript: api.setDefaultRole(role: string): string The role every player has unless somebody gives them another. This is how a mod makes a story: the stock "visitor" role is chat and interact with no build, so the valley stays as its author left it while doors, chests and levers still work. api.set_default_role("visitor") # a world to walk through, not one to change Story mode needed no new capability in the end: "build" has been a permission since roles existed, the engine already refuses a break or a place without it, tells the player why (once every three seconds, not once a click) and puts the block back on the client that predicted it. All that was missing was a mod being able to say which role people start in. Returns "" or why not. See also: exists
docs.title: api.set_default_role

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_weather(weather_name: String, def: Dictionary) -> int JavaScript: api.registerWeather(weatherName, def) Registers a kind of weather. The engine draws it and keeps everyone in the same sky; the mod decides what it looks like and when it happens. api.register_weather("rain", { "emitter": {"amount": 220, "lifetime": 1.1, "speed": [16, 20], "direction": [0, -1, 0], "spread": 3, "size": [0.05, 0.05], "colors": ["#9fc4e8aa"], "shape": "box", "extents": [18, 1, 18]}, "sound": "rain", "sky_tint": "#6a7686", "light_scale": 0.72}) emitter is the same shape as an effect's (see register_effect), drawn continuously above whoever is out in it. sound loops while it falls, sky_tint colours the sky, light_scale darkens the world, fog closes the distance in. When it rains is not here. That is a mod's decision and games want wildly different answers - a survival world on a timer, a story where the storm arrives because the story says so. api.register_weather("haze", {"display_name": "Haze", "darkness": 0.2, "particles": "puff"}) See also: qualified , register , reload
docs.title: api.register_weather

docs.text: GDScript: api.set_weather(weather_name: String, options := {}) -> void JavaScript: api.setWeather(weatherName, options) Starts weather for everyone, or stops it with "". seconds of 0 leaves it until something changes it.
docs.title: api.set_weather

docs.text: GDScript: api.get_weather() -> Dictionary JavaScript: api.getWeather() What the sky is doing: {name, intensity}. name is "" when it is clear. See also: register_music , weather_state
docs.title: api.get_weather

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_music(track_name: String, file: String, options := {}) -> int JavaScript: api.registerMusic(name: string, file: string, options: { attribution: string; volume?: number; loop?: boolean }): number Registers a music track. attribution is required: say who made it and under what licence. api.register_music("valley", "music/valley.ogg", { "attribution": "Kevin MacLeod - Meadow (CC0)", "volume": 0.8}) The audio is registered as a lazy asset, so it does not join the download a player waits through to get in; it arrives quietly afterwards and the track starts when it is ready. Nothing is ever held up waiting for music, which is the whole reason the lazy lane exists. Attribution is required rather than encouraged because whoever runs a server is redistributing this to their children and anyone else who joins, and a track whose source nobody wrote down is one whose licence nobody can check later. /music shows the credits in game. api.register_music("daylight", "music/daylight.ogg", {"volume": 0.9, "attribution": credit}) See also: register , register_asset , reload
docs.title: api.register_music

docs.text: GDScript: api.play_music(player, track_name: String, options := {}) -> void JavaScript: api.playMusic(player: Player | null, name: string, options?: { fade?: number; restart?: boolean }): void Starts a track for one player, or for everybody when player is null. Playing the track that is already playing does nothing, so this is safe to call every time the biome or the time of day changes - which is how a mod will actually want to use it. options: {fade (seconds to cross over, default 2.0), restart (start again even if it is already playing, default false)}. api.play_music(ev.player, "night" if api.get_daylight() < 0.3 else "daylight", {"fade": 6.0})) See also: send_music
docs.title: api.play_music

docs.text: GDScript: api.stop_music(player, options := {}) -> void JavaScript: api.stopMusic(player: Player | null, options?: { fade?: number }): void Fades the music out for one player, or for everybody when player is null. See also: send_music
docs.title: api.stop_music

docs.text: GDScript: api.set_map_marker(player, marker_id: String, marker: Dictionary) -> void JavaScript: api.setMapMarker(player, markerId, marker) Puts a marker on a player's map and compass (it stays until removed). marker = {label, position, color, dimension}. Markers are per player, so a home or a grave only shows to whoever it belongs to. dimension ("" = the ordinary world) hides it while they are somewhere else. See also: dimension_of
docs.title: api.set_map_marker

docs.text: GDScript: api.clear_map_marker(player, marker_id: String) -> void JavaScript: api.clearMapMarker(player, markerId) Takes a marker off a player's map.
docs.title: api.clear_map_marker

docs.text: GDScript: api.set_world_marker(marker_id: String, marker: Dictionary) -> void JavaScript: api.setWorldMarker(markerId, marker) Puts a marker on everyone's map and compass (a village, a shared base, an event). Saved with the world. marker = {label, position, color, dimension} ("" = the ordinary world).
docs.title: api.set_world_marker

docs.text: GDScript: api.clear_world_marker(marker_id: String) -> void JavaScript: api.clearWorldMarker(markerId) Takes a marker off everyone's map.
docs.title: api.clear_world_marker

docs.text: GDScript: api.open_bag(player, slot: int) -> bool JavaScript: api.openBag(player, slot) Opens the bag a player is carrying in one of their own inventory slots. A bag is an item whose definition names a container type, the way a chest block does. Its contents live in the item's own data, so it holds what it holds wherever it goes - into a chest, onto the floor, into somebody else's hands - with no bookkeeping to keep the two in step. api.register_item("satchel", {"display_name": "Satchel", "container": "proving:satchel"}) api.on("item_use", func(ev): api.open_bag(ev.player, ev.player.selected_slot)) A bag cannot be put inside a bag; the engine refuses it, because a container that can contain itself is a duplication bug waiting for somebody to find it. if not api.open_bag(player, player.selected_slot): See also: open_item , shared_store
docs.title: api.open_bag

docs.text: GDScript: api.shared_store(store_name: String, container_type: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.sharedStore(storeName, containerType) Declares a store that is the same contents wherever it is opened. Returns false if the container type is unknown. Whose it is, is the name's business. One vault for the server is shared_store("vault", ...) ; one each is shared_store("vault_" + p.player_id, ...) . The engine keeps a table of names, which is why it does not need to know which you meant. api.shared_store("vault", "vault") See also: declare_store
docs.title: api.shared_store

docs.text: GDScript: api.open_shared(player, store_name: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.openShared(player, storeName) Opens a shared store for a player. Declare it with shared_store first. api.open_shared(player, "vault")) See also: open_store
docs.title: api.open_shared

docs.text: GDScript: api.get_shared(store_name: String) JavaScript: api.getShared(storeName) The contents of a shared store without opening a screen, for a mod that wants to read or fill one. Returns null if it was never declared. See also: store_key
docs.title: api.get_shared

docs.text: GDScript: api.play_decal(position: Vector3, normal := Vector3i.UP, look := {}, realm_id := "") -> void JavaScript: api.playDecal(position, normal, look, realmId) Leaves a mark on the world: scorch where a blast went off, a stain under something leaking. look: {color, size, seconds} - no seconds leaves it until older marks push it out. It projects onto whatever is underneath, so it follows the shape of the ground and does not have to know what it landed on. normal turns it to lie on a wall rather than the floor. api.play_decal(at - Vector3(0, 0.5, 0), Vector3i.UP, {"color": "#222222", "size": 2.0}) See also: qualified , realm_of
docs.title: api.play_decal

docs.text: GDScript: api.screen_tint(player, look := {}) -> void JavaScript: api.screenTint(player, look) Washes a colour over one player's view: underwater, poisoned, standing too near the fire. look: {color, strength 0-1, seconds} - no seconds holds it until it is changed or cleared, which is what "underwater" wants; seconds fades it out, which is what a flash wants. strength 0 clears it. A tint on the view , which nothing could do before - weather colours the sky and the fog, and that is not the same thing. It obeys the player's accessibility setting for flashes, because a full-screen colour is exactly what somebody may need turned down and a mod should not overrule it. api.screen_tint(player, {"color": "#3366aa", "strength": 0.3})
docs.title: api.screen_tint

docs.text: GDScript: api.play_beam(from: Vector3, to: Vector3, look := {}, realm_id := "") -> void JavaScript: api.playBeam(from, to, look, realmId) Draws a line between two places for a moment: a spell going off, an arc of lightning, a beam holding something up. look: color, width, seconds, sag (0 is straight, higher hangs). Its own call rather than an effect with a shape, because an emitter says "from here, outwards" and can never say "from here to there". api.play_beam(at + Vector3(0, 1, 0), at + Vector3(0, 1, 6), {"color": "#88ddff", "seconds": 0.5}) See also: qualified , realm_of
docs.title: api.play_beam

docs.text: GDScript: api.found_company(company_name: String, founder_id: String) -> int JavaScript: api.foundCompany(companyName, founderId) A group of players that things can belong to: a guild, a town, a crew. Returns its id, or 0. Separate from plots on purpose , though a plot is the obvious thing for one to own: plenty of servers want groups without land, and plenty want land without groups. What a rank means is yours - the engine only keeps who is in what and what they are called, and holds one opinion of its own: the last owner cannot leave or be demoted, because a company nobody owns cannot be wound up and everything it holds becomes unreachable. See also: create
docs.title: api.found_company

docs.text: GDScript: api.disband_company(company_id: int) -> bool JavaScript: api.disbandCompany(companyId) See also: disband
docs.title: api.disband_company

docs.text: GDScript: api.set_company_rank(company_id: int, player_id: String, rank: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.setCompanyRank(companyId, playerId, rank) Ranks are "member", "officer", "owner", least to most. See also: set_rank
docs.title: api.set_company_rank

docs.text: GDScript: api.remove_from_company(company_id: int, player_id: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.removeFromCompany(companyId, playerId)
docs.title: api.remove_from_company

docs.text: GDScript: api.company_rank(company_id: int, player_id: String) -> String JavaScript: api.companyRank(companyId, playerId) See also: rank_of
docs.title: api.company_rank

docs.text: GDScript: api.company_at_least(company_id: int, player_id: String, rank: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.companyAtLeast(companyId, playerId, rank) Whether somebody is at least this rank. See also: at_least
docs.title: api.company_at_least

docs.text: GDScript: api.companies_of(who) -> Array JavaScript: api.companiesOf(who) Every company somebody is in: [{id, name, rank}]. See also: of_player
docs.title: api.companies_of

docs.text: GDScript: api.claim_plot(from: Vector3i, to: Vector3i, options := {}) -> int JavaScript: api.claimPlot(from, to, options) Marks out a piece of ground with an owner. The engine asks before letting anybody change a block inside it, on every edit path at once. Returns the plot id, or 0 - and plot_problem() says why. api.claim_plot(from, to, {"owner": player.player_id, "name": "Rowan's garden"}) api.claim_plot(from, to, {"company": guild_id}) What may be claimed, how much and what it costs are yours. The engine stores a box and an owner and enforces it. Plots may not overlap - two owners of one block is a question with no good answer - and admins are never stopped, because somebody has to be able to put right a plot marked over a village. See also: claim , qualified
docs.title: api.claim_plot

docs.text: GDScript: api.release_plot(plot_id: int) -> bool JavaScript: api.releasePlot(plotId) See also: release
docs.title: api.release_plot

docs.text: GDScript: api.plot_problem() -> String JavaScript: api.plotProblem()
docs.title: api.plot_problem

docs.text: GDScript: api.plot_at(position: Vector3i, realm_id := "") -> Dictionary JavaScript: api.plotAt(position, realmId) The plot a block is in, or {}. See also: at , qualified
docs.title: api.plot_at

docs.text: GDScript: api.may_build(player, position: Vector3i, realm_id := "") -> bool JavaScript: api.mayBuild(player, position, realmId) Whether this player may change a block here. The engine already asks this itself before any edit; this is for a mod that wants to check before offering something. See also: at , may_build_in , qualified
docs.title: api.may_build

docs.text: GDScript: api.add_plot_member(plot_id: int, player_id: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.addPlotMember(plotId, playerId) See also: add_member
docs.title: api.add_plot_member

docs.text: GDScript: api.remove_plot_member(plot_id: int, player_id: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.removePlotMember(plotId, playerId) See also: remove_member
docs.title: api.remove_plot_member

docs.text: GDScript: api.plots_of(who) -> Array JavaScript: api.plotsOf(who) Every plot somebody has a say in. See also: of_player , register_objective
docs.title: api.plots_of

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_objective(objective_name: String, def: Dictionary) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerObjective(objectiveName, def) Something a player has been asked to do: a story, a daily errand, a contract, a delivery. api.register_objective("deliver_the_post", {"display_name": "The Post", "steps": [{"text": "Take the letter to Bramble"}, {"text": "Bring her answer back"}]}) Not a tutorial and not a milestone , both of which exist already. A tutorial teaches, starts itself and is the same for everybody; a milestone notices something that already happened. An objective is given, can be refused, runs alongside others, has steps in an order, and can be abandoned. The engine never decides whether a step is done. It counts, remembers and tells you; you watch whatever event means "they did it" and call advance_objective. Otherwise the engine would have to learn what delivering a letter is. api.register_objective("errand", {"display_name": "An Errand", "steps": [{"text": "Go and see"}, {"text": "Come back", "count": 2}]}) See also: register
docs.title: api.register_objective

docs.text: GDScript: api.give_objective(player, objective_name: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.giveObjective(player, objectiveName) Gives one to a player. False if they have it, have finished one that does not repeat, or are carrying as many as they may. See also: give , qualified
docs.title: api.give_objective

docs.text: GDScript: api.advance_objective(player, objective_name: String, amount := 1) -> bool JavaScript: api.advanceObjective(player, objectiveName, amount) Counts towards the step they are on; finishing the last step fires objective_done , which is where a reward belongs - the engine has no idea what a reward would be. See also: advance , qualified
docs.title: api.advance_objective

docs.text: GDScript: api.abandon_objective(player, objective_name: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.abandonObjective(player, objectiveName) See also: abandon , qualified
docs.title: api.abandon_objective

docs.text: GDScript: api.objectives_of(player) -> Array JavaScript: api.objectivesOf(player) What they are doing now: [{name, display_name, step, of, text, progress, needed}]. See also: active_for
docs.title: api.objectives_of

docs.text: GDScript: api.has_objective(player, objective_name: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.hasObjective(player, objectiveName) See also: qualified
docs.title: api.has_objective

docs.text: GDScript: api.objective_finished(player, objective_name: String) -> int JavaScript: api.objectiveFinished(player, objectiveName) How many times they have finished it. See also: finished , qualified , register_character
docs.title: api.objective_finished

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_character(character_name: String, def: Dictionary) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerCharacter(characterName, def) Somebody to talk to: a villager, a guide, a shopkeeper, a character in a story. api.register_character("bramble", {"display_name": "Bramble", "color": "#ffd166", "lines": { "start": {"text": "Oh - somebody. I saw your fire from the ridge.", "options": [ {"text": "What have you got?", "sells": "bramble_wares"}, {"text": "Need anything doing?", "gives": "deliver_the_post"}, {"text": "Who are you?", "goes_to": "who"}]}, "who": {"text": "Bramble. I mend things, mostly.", "options": [{"text": "I see", "goes_to": "start"}]}}}) The engine draws the conversation, so every character in every mod looks and works the same way - a child who has learned to talk to one has learned to talk to all of them. It knows a conversation is lines with options and nothing else about what any of it means. goes_to moves to another line, gives hands over an objective, sells opens a shop, and does fires character_choice for anything else at all. api.register_character("keeper", {"display_name": "The Keeper", "color": "#ffd166", "lines": { "start": {"text": "You again.", "options": [ {"text": "What have you got?", "sells": "stall"}, {"text": "Anything to do?", "gives": "errand"}, {"text": "Who are you?", "goes_to": "who"}, {"text": "Nothing", "does": "wave"}]}, "who": {"text": "The keeper of this place.", "options": [{"text": "I see", "goes_to": "start"}]}, "settled": {"text": "Settled in, then."}}}) See also: register
docs.title: api.register_character

docs.text: GDScript: api.talk_to(player, character_name: String, options := {}) -> bool JavaScript: api.talkTo(player, characterName, options) Starts a conversation, usually from an entity_interact handler. line is where to open - which is yours, because whether somebody has settled in or is still a stranger is a fact about your story and not about conversations. See also: qualified , talk
docs.title: api.talk_to

docs.text: GDScript: api.has_met(player, character_name: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.hasMet(player, characterName) Whether this player has ever spoken to them, which is most of what "we have met before" needs. See also: qualified , register_shop
docs.title: api.has_met

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_shop(shop_name: String, def: Dictionary) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerShop(shopName, def) Somewhere to buy and sell: a village stall, a pedlar, a vending machine. api.register_shop("bramble_wares", {"display_name": "Bramble's Wares", "offers": [ {"item": "rope", "count": 2, "price": 4, "ledger": "coins", "stock": 10, "restock": 600.0}, {"item": "apple", "price": 1, "ledger": "coins", "sells": true}, {"item": "lantern", "cost": [{"item": "iron_bar", "count": 2}, {"item": "coal"}]}]}) Coins are not assumed. A price is a number out of a ledger, or a list of items, or both, so a game with no money barters perfectly well. sells: true turns an offer round - the player hands the item over and is paid for it. Stock is the part that matters. A shop with unlimited everything is a creative menu with an extra step; stock and restock are what make the blacksmith who has three swords this week somewhere worth going back to. Leave stock out for an offer that never runs dry. api.register_shop("stall", {"display_name": "The Stall", "offers": [ {"item": "proving:token", "count": 2, "price": 5, "ledger": "coins", "stock": 3, "restock": 30.0}, {"item": "proving:rock", "count": 4, "cost": [{"item": "proving:token", "count": 1}]}, {"item": "proving:plain", "price": 1, "ledger": "coins", "sells": true}]}) See also: register
docs.title: api.register_shop

docs.text: GDScript: api.show_shop(player, shop_name: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.showShop(player, shopName) Opens the stall. Drawn by the engine, like a conversation, so every shop works the same way. See also: qualified , show
docs.title: api.show_shop

docs.text: GDScript: api.shop_trade(player, shop_name: String, index: int) -> bool JavaScript: api.shopTrade(player, shopName, index) Does one trade directly, for a shop with no panel - a vending block, a delivery chute. False when it cannot happen, and shop_problem says why in words a child can read. See also: qualified , trade
docs.title: api.shop_trade

docs.text: GDScript: api.shop_problem() -> String JavaScript: api.shopProblem()
docs.title: api.shop_problem

docs.text: GDScript: api.shop_offers(player, shop_name: String) -> Array JavaScript: api.shopOffers(player, shopName) What is on the shelves: [{index, item, name, count, price, ledger, cost, sells, left, can}]. See also: offers_for , qualified , register_entity , set_nameplate
docs.title: api.shop_offers

docs.text: GDScript: api.set_nameplate(target, spec := {}) -> bool JavaScript: api.setNameplate(target, spec) The label over a thing's head: what it is called, how hurt it is, and anything you want to add. api.set_nameplate(mob, {"lines": ["Wants: wheat"], "show_health": true}) api.register_entity("cow", {..., "nameplate": {"show_health": true}}) Creatures are quiet by default - a field of forty sheep each wearing a label is worse than no labels - so a type only gets one if its definition says so, or a mod sets one on a particular creature. Players always have their name. spec merges with what is already there, so you can add a line without knowing whether health is being shown. Keys: name, lines (up to 4), show_health, color, range, hidden. See also: set_plate
docs.title: api.set_nameplate

docs.text: GDScript: api.nameplate_of(target) -> Dictionary JavaScript: api.nameplateOf(target) What is over its head now, defaults included. See also: plate_of
docs.title: api.nameplate_of

docs.text: GDScript: api.clear_nameplate(target) -> bool JavaScript: api.clearNameplate(target) See also: float_text , follow
docs.title: api.clear_nameplate

docs.text: GDScript: api.float_text(text: String, position: Vector3, options := {}, realm_id := "") -> void JavaScript: api.floatText(text, position, options, realmId) A word that floats in the world for a moment and then goes: the damage off a hit, "+3" over a chest, a name over a thing. api.float_text("12", position, {"color": "#ff6666", "follow": mob}) Transient on purpose - nothing is stored and nobody has to clean it up. It is drawn through walls, because a number that vanishes behind a post is a number nobody can read. options: color, seconds, rise (how far it drifts up), size, follow (a player or entity it sticks to). api.float_text("%d" % roundi(was - float(ev.health)), e.body.position + Vector3(0, e.def.height * 0.9, 0), {"color": "#ffd166", "follow": e, "seconds": 0.8})) See also: qualified , register_entity
docs.title: api.float_text

docs.text: GDScript: api.mount(player, entity) -> bool JavaScript: api.mount(player, entity) Puts a player on a vehicle - an entity whose type has a vehicle block. Returns false when it is full, too far away, or they are already riding something. api.register_entity("boat", {"kind": "mob", "model": "models/boat.glb", "ai": {"preset": "none"}, "vehicle": {"seats": 2, "speed": 6.0, "turn_speed": 3.0, "floats": true}}) A rider stops simulating themselves: their position comes from the vehicle and their input becomes steering - throttle forward and back, and the vehicle turns towards wherever they are looking. Sneak gets off. The player's own physics is untouched, which is why riding cannot break walking. See also: config_of , is_alive , riders_of , tell_riding
docs.title: api.mount

docs.text: GDScript: api.dismount(player, to = null) -> bool JavaScript: api.dismount(player, to) Takes a player off. to is where to put them down; by default beside the vehicle. See also: riders_of , tell_riding
docs.title: api.dismount

docs.text: GDScript: api.riding(player) JavaScript: api.riding(player) The entity a player is riding, or null.
docs.title: api.riding

docs.text: GDScript: api.riders_of(entity) -> Array JavaScript: api.ridersOf(entity) Who is aboard, as player ids. See also: order , register_order
docs.title: api.riders_of

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_order(order_name: String, def := {}) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerOrder(orderName, def) Something a tamed creature can be told to do. api.register_order("fetch", {"display_name": "Fetch that", "behavior": "my_mod:fetch"}) api.order(dog, "fetch") Taming already gave a companion three of its four parts - it follows, it is owned, and it does not despawn. Taking instruction was one boolean, sitting , toggled by right-clicking, which runs out the moment there are three things to say. Three orders are the engine's own, because all three are about where : engine:follow , engine:stay and engine:guard . Anything else maps to a behaviour registered with register_mob_behavior - the engine sets the order, your behaviour decides what it looks like. Right-clicking a companion opens the order panel, drawn by the engine. Restrict what a particular creature may be told by handling companion_orders and editing orders . api.register_order("forage", {"display_name": "Forage here", "behavior": "proving:forage"}) See also: at , qualified , register
docs.title: api.register_order

docs.text: GDScript: api.order(entity, order_name: String, options := {}) -> bool JavaScript: api.order(entity, orderName, options) Tells a creature something. options: at (where, for orders that need a place; defaults to where it is standing). See also: give , now , qualified
docs.title: api.order

docs.text: GDScript: api.order_of(entity) -> String JavaScript: api.orderOf(entity) What it is being told to do now ("engine:follow" when nobody has said otherwise). "score": func(brain): return 0.2 if api.order_of(brain.entity) == "proving:forage" else 0.0,
docs.title: api.order_of

docs.text: GDScript: api.show_orders(player, entity) -> bool JavaScript: api.showOrders(player, entity) Opens the order panel for a player, as right-clicking their own companion does. See also: place_field , register_field , show
docs.title: api.show_orders

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_field(field_name: String, def: Dictionary) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerField(fieldName, def) Ground that does something to whoever stands in it, for a while: a pool of fire left where a boss landed, gas from a cracked pipe, the warmth of a campfire, a healing circle in a village. api.register_field("fire_pool", {"radius": 3.0, "seconds": 10.0, "effect": "engine:flame", "tick": {"seconds": 1.0, "damage": 2.0, "cause": "fire"}, "condition": {"condition": "burning", "seconds": 4.0}}) api.place_field("fire_pool", position, {"seconds": 20.0, "owner": mob}) Called a field because plots and claims are taken - plots are ground with an owner, claims are ground kept awake. It is always visible : an invisible thing on the floor that hurts a child is not a hazard but a trick, so placing one starts a running effect. You choose which; you cannot choose none. affects is "everyone", "players" or "creatures" - not "enemies", which would mean the engine learning about sides. except_owner (on by default) keeps whoever left it out of their own fire. api.register_field("scorch", {"display_name": "Scorch", "radius": 3.0, "seconds": 8.0, "effect": "engine:smoke", "tick": {"seconds": 1.0, "damage": 1.0, "cause": "scorch"}, "condition": {"condition": "venom", "seconds": 3.0}}) See also: qualified , register
docs.title: api.register_field

docs.text: GDScript: api.place_field(field_name: String, position: Vector3, options := {}) -> int JavaScript: api.placeField(fieldName, position, options) Puts one down. options: seconds, radius, level (multiplies damage, heal and the condition's level), owner (a player or creature it will not touch), realm. Returns its id, or 0. See also: place , qualified
docs.title: api.place_field

docs.text: GDScript: api.clear_field(id: int) -> bool JavaScript: api.clearField(id)
docs.title: api.clear_field

docs.text: GDScript: api.fields_at(position: Vector3, realm_id := "") -> Array JavaScript: api.fieldsAt(position, realmId) Every field a point is inside: [{id, kind, realm, position, radius, level, seconds}]. See also: at , qualified , register_condition
docs.title: api.fields_at

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_condition(condition_name: String, def: Dictionary) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerCondition(conditionName, def) Something a player or a creature is temporarily under: swiftness, poison, a well-fed glow. api.register_condition("swiftness", {"display_name": "Swiftness", "color": "#7fd6ff", "modifiers": [{"stat": "move_speed", "amount": 0.2, "op": "multiply"}], "max_level": 3}) api.register_condition("poison", {"display_name": "Poison", "good": false, "tick": {"seconds": 1.5, "damage": 1.0, "cause": "poison"}}) Called a condition because register_effect already means particles. A condition is a stat change, or something that repeats on a timer, or both - and the timer is the part a plain timed modifier could never express, which is what poison, regeneration and burning all need. Levels multiply rather than re-describe: Swiftness II is the same modifiers doubled. stacks says what a second helping does - "strongest" (the default), "refresh" or "extend". What stays yours: what conditions exist, what brews or cures them, and what a level means. api.register_condition("venom", {"display_name": "Venom", "good": false, "color": "#89c24a", "tick": {"seconds": 1.0, "damage": 1.0, "cause": "venom"}, "max_level": 3}) See also: register
docs.title: api.register_condition

docs.text: GDScript: api.give_condition(target, condition_name: String, options := {}) -> bool JavaScript: api.giveCondition(target, conditionName, options) Gives one to a player or a creature. options: seconds (0 = until taken away), level. See also: give , qualified
docs.title: api.give_condition

docs.text: GDScript: api.clear_condition(target, condition_name: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.clearCondition(target, conditionName) See also: qualified
docs.title: api.clear_condition

docs.text: GDScript: api.clear_conditions(target, only_bad := false) -> int JavaScript: api.clearConditions(target, onlyBad) Takes everything away, or with only_bad everything unpleasant - which is the whole of what a cure is, and saves listing every affliction in the game. Returns how many went. See also: clear_all
docs.title: api.clear_conditions

docs.text: GDScript: api.has_condition(target, condition_name: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.hasCondition(target, conditionName) See also: qualified
docs.title: api.has_condition

docs.text: GDScript: api.condition_level(target, condition_name: String) -> int JavaScript: api.conditionLevel(target, conditionName) 0 when they do not have it. See also: level_of , qualified
docs.title: api.condition_level

docs.text: GDScript: api.conditions_of(target) -> Array JavaScript: api.conditionsOf(target) What they are under: [{name, display_name, color, level, good, seconds}], seconds -1 for one that does not run out. See also: of_target , register_ledger
docs.title: api.conditions_of

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_ledger(ledger_name: String, def := {}) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerLedger(ledgerName, def) A named number a player owns: coins, reputation, contribution, experience, a guild's standing. api.register_ledger("coins", {"display_name": "Coins", "min": 0}) api.register_ledger("delving", {"display_name": "Delving", "levels": [0, 50, 150, 400]}) Balances and experience are one thing here, not two. They are the same storage asked a different question - a balance is a number you care about the value of, experience is one you care about the level of - so a ledger given thresholds answers about levels as well. The engine stores a number against a player and a name and never learns that one of them is money. What a level unlocks, whether anything unlocks at all, whether coins may go negative: all yours. api.register_ledger("coins", {"display_name": "Coins", "min": 0}) See also: register
docs.title: api.register_ledger

docs.text: GDScript: api.balance_of(player, ledger_name: String) -> float JavaScript: api.balanceOf(player, ledgerName) {"type": "progress", "value": int(api.balance_of(player, "coins")), "max": 10, "color": "#6fcf97"}, See also: qualified , value_of
docs.title: api.balance_of

docs.text: GDScript: api.add_balance(player, ledger_name: String, amount: float) -> float JavaScript: api.addBalance(player, ledgerName, amount) Adds (or, with a negative amount, takes away). Returns what it ended up as, which is not always what was asked for when the ledger has a floor or a ceiling. api.add_balance(ev.player, "coins", 1.0)) See also: qualified
docs.title: api.add_balance

docs.text: GDScript: api.set_balance(player, ledger_name: String, value: float) -> float JavaScript: api.setBalance(player, ledgerName, value) See also: qualified , set_value
docs.title: api.set_balance

docs.text: GDScript: api.spend_balance(player, ledger_name: String, amount: float) -> bool JavaScript: api.spendBalance(player, ledgerName, amount) Takes amount only if there is that much. Written as one call on purpose: a shop that checks and then subtracts has a gap between the two, and this does not. See also: at , qualified , spend
docs.title: api.spend_balance

docs.text: GDScript: api.level_of(player, ledger_name: String) -> int JavaScript: api.levelOf(player, ledgerName) What level they are at (0 when the ledger has no thresholds). See also: level_for , qualified , value_of
docs.title: api.level_of

docs.text: GDScript: api.level_progress(player, ledger_name: String) -> Dictionary JavaScript: api.levelProgress(player, ledgerName) {level, value, into (0-1 through this level), needed, next} - for a bar on the screen. See also: progress_of , qualified
docs.title: api.level_progress

docs.text: GDScript: api.balances_of(player) -> Array JavaScript: api.balancesOf(player) Everything a player has any of: [{name, display_name, value, level}]. See also: all_of , register_modifier
docs.title: api.balances_of

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_modifier(modifier_name: String, def: Dictionary) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerModifier(modifierName, def) A named mark that can be put on a particular item and changes what it does - an enchantment, in your own words. api.register_modifier("keen", {"display_name": "Keen", "max_level": 3, "per_level": [{"stat": "damage", "amount": 1.0}], "applies_to": ["#base:axes"]}) applies_to names items or tags; empty means anything. The stat changes are worked out per level, and a line of lore is written into the item so its tooltip says "Keen II" without anything new on the wire. There is no hook system here on purpose. A mark that should set things alight is a mod listening to the hit event it already has and asking whether the weapon is kindled. A second way of doing what events already do would be worse than one. api.register_modifier("keen", {"display_name": "Keen", "max_level": 3, "per_level": [{"stat": "attack_damage", "amount": 1.0}], "applies_to": ["#proving:prods"]}) See also: qualified , register
docs.title: api.register_modifier

docs.text: GDScript: api.apply_modifier(item_data: Dictionary, item_name: String, modifier_name: String, level := 1) -> Dictionary JavaScript: api.applyModifier(itemData, itemName, modifierName, level) Puts a mark on an item, returning the new item data (level 0 takes it off). The item is returned unchanged if the mark does not belong on it, so a mistake gives back an item rather than a mess. See also: apply , qualified
docs.title: api.apply_modifier

docs.text: GDScript: api.modifier_level(item_data: Dictionary, modifier_name: String) -> int JavaScript: api.modifierLevel(itemData, modifierName) What level of a mark an item carries, or 0. See also: level_of , qualified
docs.title: api.modifier_level

docs.text: GDScript: api.modifiers_on(item_data: Dictionary) -> Array JavaScript: api.modifiersOn(itemData) Every mark on an item: [{name, level, display_name}]. See also: assembly_problem , marks_on
docs.title: api.modifiers_on

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_liquid(block_name: String, def := {}) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerLiquid(blockName, def) Makes a block a liquid that goes somewhere: spreads, falls, and dries up when nothing feeds it. api.register_liquid("water", {"range": 7, "falls": true, "speed": 0.25}) def: range (how many blocks from a source before it runs out), falls , speed (seconds between steps - lava is slow, which is most of what makes it frightening), shallow (a block to use once it has spread shallow_from blocks - give it a slab shape and a thin sheet looks and wades like one). The level lives in the block's state: 0 is a source and never runs out, and each block outwards is one weaker. Nothing new is written to disk or sent to clients, because states already were. api.register_liquid("slime", {"range": 4, "falls": true, "speed": 0.4, "shallow": "proving:slime_thin", "shallow_from": 2}) See also: block , is_excluded , qualified , register , register_block_tick
docs.title: api.register_liquid

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_liquid_meeting(a_name: String, b_name: String, result_name: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerLiquidMeeting(aName, bName, resultName) What forms where two different liquids meet - the black glass where lava meets water. The engine has never heard of obsidian; it only knows that two of them touching makes a third thing. api.register_liquid_meeting("slime", "proving:slime", "proving:plain") See also: block , is_excluded , qualified , register_meeting
docs.title: api.register_liquid_meeting

docs.text: GDScript: api.keep_awake(position: Vector3i, options := {}) -> int JavaScript: api.keepAwake(position, options) Keeps the world around a position awake when nobody is standing there, so a machine goes on running after its owner walks away. Returns a claim id. options: radius (chunks either side, 0-8), player_id (who to tell if it has to be paused), name (what to call the place when telling them), realm . This costs somebody something, and the engine says so. Claims are charged what their chunks actually spend in block ticks, and when they exceed the share of a tick the host allows, the dearest is paused first and its owner is told in plain words. Nothing is ever deleted - pausing stops the ticking and leaves the blocks and their contents alone. Only things that cannot be caught up need this. Crops and furnaces work out what they missed when somebody comes back; a pump feeding a network cannot, because what it did depended on the rest of the world while it was doing it. See also: qualified
docs.title: api.keep_awake

docs.text: GDScript: api.let_sleep(claim_id: int) -> bool JavaScript: api.letSleep(claimId) Stops keeping it awake.
docs.title: api.let_sleep

docs.text: GDScript: api.wake_claim(claim_id: int) -> bool JavaScript: api.wakeClaim(claimId) Lets a paused claim run again. See also: resume , set_accepts
docs.title: api.wake_claim

docs.text: GDScript: api.set_accepts(node: Dictionary, filter := {}) -> void JavaScript: api.setAccepts(node, filter) What a face will take, as items and tags. An empty filter takes anything, which is what an ordinary pipe end is; deny: true turns it inside out, which is how "everything except cobblestone" is said. api.set_accepts(node, {"tags": ["base:logs"]}) See also: key_name , node_key , qualified , tag
docs.title: api.set_accepts

docs.text: GDScript: api.stop_accepting(node: Dictionary) -> void JavaScript: api.stopAccepting(node) See also: key_name , node_key , qualified , tag
docs.title: api.stop_accepting

docs.text: GDScript: api.would_accept(from: Dictionary, item_name: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.wouldAccept(from, itemName) Whether anything connected would take this, without sending it. See also: key_name , node_key , qualified , reachable , tag
docs.title: api.would_accept

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_drive(unit_name: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerDrive(unitName) A kind of value driven through the links rather than stored in them: rotation, and anything else that means "this end turns, so that end turns". Not the same as a quantity. Power buffers, fills and runs out, and two generators on one grid add up. Rotation is a speed and a direction, it arrives the instant the shaft turns, nothing accumulates anywhere, and two sources driving one line do not add - they fight, and the engine says so rather than inventing an average nobody asked for. Gearing is not here. A gearbox is a block that reads one line and drives another at a different speed, which is a few lines in a mod - and then the engine has no opinion about what ratios exist. api.register_drive("shaft") See also: register_unit
docs.title: api.register_drive

docs.text: GDScript: api.set_drive(unit_name: String, node: Dictionary, value: float) -> void JavaScript: api.setDrive(unitName, node, value) This face drives at value - a speed, with a sign for which way round. 0 stops driving. See also: qualified , set_source , tag
docs.title: api.set_drive

docs.text: GDScript: api.driven_at(unit_name: String, node: Dictionary) -> float JavaScript: api.drivenAt(unitName, node) What a face is being driven at. Zero when nothing drives it, and zero when the line is jammed, because a jammed line does not turn. See also: qualified , tag , value_at
docs.title: api.driven_at

docs.text: GDScript: api.drive_jammed(unit_name: String, node: Dictionary) -> bool JavaScript: api.driveJammed(unitName, node) Whether two sources are fighting over the line this face is on. See also: jammed_at , qualified , tag
docs.title: api.drive_jammed

docs.text: GDScript: api.on_driven(unit_name: String, handler: Callable) -> void JavaScript: api.onDriven(unitName, handler) Told when what a face is driven at changes: {realm, position, face, unit, value, jammed}. See also: on_changed , qualified
docs.title: api.on_driven

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_unit(unit_name: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerUnit(unitName) A kind of quantity that moves along links: power, steam, water, mana. The engine keeps them apart by name and learns nothing else about any of them. api.register_unit("power")
docs.title: api.register_unit

docs.text: GDScript: api.set_supply(unit_name: String, node: Dictionary, amount: float) -> void JavaScript: api.setSupply(unitName, node, amount) This face offers this much per second (0 to stop). A generator running; a tank draining. See also: key_name , node_key , qualified , tag
docs.title: api.set_supply

docs.text: GDScript: api.set_demand(unit_name: String, node: Dictionary, amount: float) -> void JavaScript: api.setDemand(unitName, node, amount) This face wants this much per second (0 to stop asking). See also: key_name , node_key , qualified , tag
docs.title: api.set_demand

docs.text: GDScript: api.received(unit_name: String, node: Dictionary) -> float JavaScript: api.received(unitName, node) What a face is actually receiving, which is not always what it asked for. See also: key_name , node_key , qualified , tag
docs.title: api.received

docs.text: GDScript: api.on_received(unit_name: String, handler: Callable) -> void JavaScript: api.onReceived(unitName, handler) Told when what a face receives changes: {realm, position, face, unit, wanted, got}. What a shortfall means is yours to decide. The engine says "you asked for twenty and you have seven" and has no opinion about whether that is a furnace running slowly, a lamp going dim or a pump stopping dead. When there is not enough to go round everybody gets the same fraction of what they asked for, so a grid under load dims all over rather than failing in an order nobody can see. See also: qualified , register_link_kind
docs.title: api.on_received

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_link_kind(kind_name: String, def := {}) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerLinkKind(kindName, def) A kind of connection a player can lay: a cable, a pipe, an aerial. api.register_link_kind("cable", {"span": 12, "item": "base:copper_wire", "draw": "cable"}) api.register_link_kind("aerial", {"wireless": true, "span": 48, "crosses_realms": true}) def: span (how far it reaches), item (what a block of it costs to lay), draw - "cable" sags, "pipe" is rigid and wants a shorter span, "" draws nothing - wireless (nothing drawn, no clear line needed), crosses_realms (wireless only; a cable is a physical thing and cannot run through the gap between worlds), needs_air , per_node (how many may meet at one face). A node is a face of a block, so a machine can take power in one side and push items out of another. Raise the reach of a particular connector by handling the link_reach event - that is where an upgrade or a better aerial belongs, rather than in the kind itself. api.register_link_kind("cable", {"span": 10.0, "needs_air": true, "draw": "cable", "color": "#c2703c"}) See also: link_problem , register_kind
docs.title: api.register_link_kind

docs.text: GDScript: api.link(kind_name: String, a: Dictionary, b: Dictionary) -> int JavaScript: api.link(kindName, a, b) Joins two faces. Each end is {realm, position, face} - realm "" is the world a server starts with, face is 0..5 (up, down, north, south, west, east). Returns the link id, or 0; when it is 0, link_problem() says why in a sentence a player can be shown. See also: qualified , tag
docs.title: api.link

docs.text: GDScript: api.link_problem() -> String JavaScript: api.linkProblem() Why the last link() was refused.
docs.title: api.link_problem

docs.text: GDScript: api.link_refused(kind_name: String, a: Dictionary, b: Dictionary) -> String JavaScript: api.linkRefused(kindName, a, b) Whether two faces could be joined, without joining them: "" means yes, anything else is the reason. See also: qualified , tag , why_not
docs.title: api.link_refused

docs.text: GDScript: api.unlink(id: int, why := "removed") -> bool JavaScript: api.unlink(id, why) Removes a link by id. See also: cut
docs.title: api.unlink

docs.text: GDScript: api.links_at(position: Vector3i, realm_id := "") -> Array JavaScript: api.linksAt(position, realmId) Every link touching a block, as ids. See also: at_block , qualified
docs.title: api.links_at

docs.text: GDScript: api.tag(tag_name: String, names: Array) -> void JavaScript: api.tag(tagName, names) Puts blocks or items into a named group: "any log", "any ore", "anything a pipe may carry". api.tag("logs", ["base:oak_log", "base:birch_log"]) # in base: defines base:logs api.tag("base:logs", ["cherry:cherry_log"]) # elsewhere: adds to base:logs A bare name is your own mod's, as everywhere else here; writing it out in full always means exactly what it says. Adding to another mod's tag is the point - a mod that adds a tree can put its wood in base:logs and every recipe the base game wrote for logs accepts it, without the base game knowing that mod exists. A tag in a namespace no installed mod owns is kept and warned about rather than refused, so a mod that integrates with another when it happens to be there does not have to guard every call. api.tag("currency", ["proving:token"]) See also: qualified
docs.title: api.tag

docs.text: GDScript: api.tagged(tag_name: String) -> Array JavaScript: api.tagged(tagName) The names in a tag (empty if nothing has defined it). See also: names_in , qualified
docs.title: api.tagged

docs.text: GDScript: api.has_tag(name: String, tag_name: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.hasTag(name, tagName) Whether a block or item name is in a tag. Reads as "does this thing have this tag", which is why the thing comes first here and the tag comes first in tag and tagged . Both arguments are strings, so getting them the wrong way round used to return a quiet false and a mod that simply never matched anything. Now it says so. (2026-09-20) See also: exists , qualified
docs.title: api.has_tag

docs.text: GDScript: api.tags_of(name: String) -> Array JavaScript: api.tagsOf(name) Every tag a block or item is in. See also: qualified
docs.title: api.tags_of

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_signal(block_name: String, handler: Callable) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerSignal(blockName, handler) Tells handler(ctx) when the level arriving at a block of this type changes: a door that should open, a lamp that should light, a machine that should start. ctx = {position, block, level, previous, realm}. Signals are three block keys and this one call. A block emits ( signal: 15 in its definition, or set_signal for a lever that is only sometimes on), a block carries ( signal_carry: true , one level weaker each block, so fifteen blocks and it is gone), and a block listens - this. Gates, delays, inverters, latches and repeaters are blocks you write , each one listening here and emitting with set_signal. The engine has no opinion about what logic looks like, because a puzzle game and a factory want different answers and it is not the engine's business to pick. api.register_signal("core", func(ctx): api.set_block_data(ctx.position, {"level": int(ctx.level)})) See also: block , is_excluded , qualified , register
docs.title: api.register_signal

docs.text: GDScript: api.set_signal(position: Vector3i, level: int, realm_id := "") -> void JavaScript: api.setSignal(position, level, realmId) Makes the block at position emit level (0 to 15; 0 stops it). For a lever being flipped, a plate being stood on, or a gate of your own working out what it should be saying. api.set_signal(ev.position, 15 if api.signal_at(ev.position) == 0 else 0)) See also: qualified , register_instance , set_source
docs.title: api.set_signal

docs.text: GDScript: api.signal_at(position: Vector3i, realm_id := "") -> int JavaScript: api.signalAt(position, realmId) The strongest level arriving at a position from anything touching it. See also: qualified , reaching , register_instance
docs.title: api.signal_at

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_instance(kind_name: String, def := {}) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerInstance(kindName, def) Declares a kind of private, throwaway space: a dungeon, a puzzle room, an arena. An instance is a realm with a lifetime - the same separate world dimensions already give you, but made on demand and thrown away when it empties. Nothing in one is written to disk. api.register_instance("dungeon", {"generator": Rooms.new(), "empty_seconds": 30, "max_players": 4}) def: {generator, passes, empty_seconds, max_players, display_name}. Without a generator the space is empty air, which is what a mod that builds its own room wants. api.register_instance("trial", {"display_name": "The Trial", "empty_seconds": 5.0, "max_players": 2}) See also: register
docs.title: api.register_instance

docs.text: GDScript: api.open_instance(kind_name: String, options := {}) -> String JavaScript: api.openInstance(kindName, options) Opens one and returns its id, or "" if it could not be opened. options: {seed, data (anything you want to keep with it; read it back with instance_data )}. var run: String = api.open_instance("trial", {"data": {"opened_for": player.name}}) See also: open
docs.title: api.open_instance

docs.text: GDScript: api.enter_instance(player, instance_id: String, position: Vector3) -> bool JavaScript: api.enterInstance(player, instanceId, position) Sends a player in, remembering where they were so leave_instance can put them back. api.enter_instance(player, run, Vector3(0.5, 66, 0.5)) See also: enter
docs.title: api.enter_instance

docs.text: GDScript: api.leave_instance(player) -> bool JavaScript: api.leaveInstance(player) Puts a player back where they were before they entered. api.leave_instance(player) See also: leave
docs.title: api.leave_instance

docs.text: GDScript: api.close_instance(instance_id: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.closeInstance(instanceId) Closes one now: everybody inside goes back and the space is thrown away. An instance also closes itself once it has been empty for its kind's empty_seconds . See also: close
docs.title: api.close_instance

docs.text: GDScript: api.instance_of(player) -> String JavaScript: api.instanceOf(player) The instance a player is in, or "". var here: String = api.instance_of(player)
docs.title: api.instance_of

docs.text: GDScript: api.instance_data(instance_id: String) -> Dictionary JavaScript: api.instanceData(instanceId) What you kept with an instance when you opened it. See also: add_ore_pass , add_realm , data_of , decorate
docs.title: api.instance_data

docs.text: GDScript: api.add_realm(realm_id: String, options := {}) -> Object JavaScript: api.addRealm(realmId, options) Adds another world to this server, reached through a portal. Call it while the mod is setting up. var deep := api.add_realm("emberdeep", {"name": "The Emberdeep", "generator": MyCaves.new()}) options: name (shown when travelling), generator (as set_world_generator, but for this world), passes (objects with decorate(chunk, seed), as ore passes are), seed (by default derived from the world's seed and this realm's name, so it is stable but not the same terrain as the overworld). Ores, biomes and features go in with the realm's id: api.add_ore_pass({...}, "emberdeep") . Returns the realm, or null if the name is taken. The id is qualified with the mod's own name, so two mods may both have an "underworld" without meeting. A realm costs nothing until somebody is standing in it: an empty one is not ticked at all (see docs/roadmap.md, "How much of the world is running"). To send somebody there: a portal block whose block data is {portal: {realm: " :emberdeep"}}, or send_to_realm. What the world is made of is the generator's business, and what it means is yours. api.add_realm("deep", {"display_name": "The Deep", "generator": "void"}) See also: attach , reload , set_storage , start
docs.title: api.add_realm

docs.text: GDScript: api.realm_of(player) -> String JavaScript: api.realmOf(player) Which world a player is standing in, as the id add_realm was given ("" is the one a server starts with). Positions mean nothing without it: every world has a block at the same coordinates. var realm_id: String = api.realm_of(player)
docs.title: api.realm_of

docs.text: GDScript: api.send_to_realm(player, realm_id: String, position: Vector3) -> bool JavaScript: api.sendToRealm(player, realmId, position) Moves a player to another world, standing at position . Returns false if there is no such world, or they are already in it. Cancellable by a mod through the player_realm_change event, which may also change where they come out. See also: ensure_area_loaded , generate , index , links_for , qualified , realm_of
docs.title: api.send_to_realm

docs.text: GDScript: api.set_wind(degrees: float, strength := 0.5, seconds := 0.0) -> void JavaScript: api.setWind(degrees, strength, seconds) Sets the wind: degrees clockwise from north, strength 0 (still) to 1 (a gale), seconds 0 for until something says otherwise - the same shape as set_weather . Wind is visual: it leans the grass, drags the clouds and slants the rain. Nothing in the simulation depends on it, so a mod may move it as freely as it likes. While a mod holds it the engine stops drifting it on its own. api.set_wind(240.0, 0.85)
docs.title: api.set_wind

docs.text: GDScript: api.get_wind() -> Dictionary JavaScript: api.getWind() The wind right now: {angle, strength} . The gusts a player actually sees are worked out on each client, so this is the average rather than the instant. See also: wind_state
docs.title: api.get_wind

docs.text: GDScript: api.content_conflicts() -> Array JavaScript: api.contentConflicts() Content two mods both claim: [{kind ("name" | "ore" | "biome"), detail, mods}]. The engine reports these and never resolves them, because every one can be deliberate - a second kind of copper may be the whole point of your mod. detail is a sentence naming both sides. A pack or a game can use this to refuse to ship, or to print a warning of its own.
docs.title: api.content_conflicts

docs.text: GDScript: api.sources_of(item_id: int) -> Array JavaScript: api.sourcesOf(itemId) Everywhere an item comes from that is not a recipe: blocks that drop it, creatures that drop it, loot tables that hold it, ore in the ground. Returns [{kind, from, detail, chance}] with the reliable sources first. kind is one of "block", "creature", "container", "ground" or "other". Mostly derived, not declared. The engine already knows every loot table, every block's drops, every creature's drops and every ore pass, so a mod that registered a creature with drops has already said where that item comes from - being asked to say it again in a second registry is how the two fall out of step. See also: chance_of , describe , kind_of , of_item
docs.title: api.sources_of

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_source(item_name: String, source: Dictionary) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerSource(itemName, source) Declares a source nothing can infer: traded by somebody, washed up after a storm, given as a reward. detail is shown to a player, so write it as a sentence. source: {kind ("block"|"creature"|"container"|"ground"|"other"), from, detail, chance}. api.register_source("proving:token", {"kind": "other", "from": "the keeper", "detail": "handed over for a favour", "chance": 0.5}) See also: declare , item
docs.title: api.register_source

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_milestone(milestone_name: String, def: Dictionary) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerMilestone(milestoneName, def) A milestone: something a player has done, remembered for the life of the world and paid out once (see engine/server/milestones.gd). Goals are written exactly as tutorial goals are - {type, target, count}, type being an event goal (break, place, craft, kill, ...) or "event" - but the count is a lifetime total. No target means anything of that kind counts. {title, description, goal, icon, order, secret (hidden until reached), announce (tell everyone), reward: {items: [[item, count]], cosmetic}}. The usual reward is a cosmetic, because a cosmetic is something other players can see. Names without ":" are this mod's. api.register_milestone("first_stone", {"display_name": "First Stone", "goal": {"type": "break", "target": ["proving:rock"]}}) See also: qualified , register
docs.title: api.register_milestone

docs.text: GDScript: api.milestone_reached(player, milestone_name: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.milestoneReached(player, milestoneName) Whether a player has reached a milestone, for gating something behind it. See also: qualified , reached
docs.title: api.milestone_reached

docs.text: GDScript: api.set_ugc_policy(values: Dictionary) -> void JavaScript: api.setUgcPolicy(values: { enabled?: boolean; accept?: "auto" | "trusted" | "approval" | "off"; kinds?: ("skin" | "accessory" | "model")[]; library?: boolean; max_per_player?: number; max_bytes_per_player?: number; report_hide?: number }): void How this server treats player creations (engine/server/ugc.gd): {enabled, accept: "auto" | "trusted" | "approval" | "off", kinds: ["skin", "accessory", "model"], library (others may wear approved ones), max_per_player, max_bytes_per_player}. Saved with the world. See also: set_policy
docs.title: api.set_ugc_policy

docs.text: GDScript: api.ugc_list(filter := "approved") -> Array JavaScript: api.ugcList(filter?: "pending" | "reported" | "approved" | "rejected" | "removed" | "all"): Record<string, unknown>[] Player creations for review or rewards: filter pending | reported | approved | rejected | removed | all. Each: {id, manifest {kind, category, name, author, author_name}, status, reason, reports, uploaded_by, size}. See also: review_list
docs.title: api.ugc_list

docs.text: GDScript: api.ugc_get(id: String) -> Dictionary JavaScript: api.ugcGet(id) One creation's record, or {}.
docs.title: api.ugc_get

docs.text: GDScript: api.ugc_set_status(id: String, status: String, reason := "") -> bool JavaScript: api.ugcSetStatus(id, status, reason) Approves, rejects (hidden; the author may upload a fixed version) or removes (blocked for good) a creation. See also: set_status
docs.title: api.ugc_set_status

docs.text: GDScript: api.ugc_report(player, id: String, reason := "other", details := "") -> String JavaScript: api.ugcReport(player, id, reason, details) Files a report as a player (e.g. from a mod's own report button). See also: report
docs.title: api.ugc_report

docs.text: GDScript: api.ugc_trust(player_id: String, on := true) -> void JavaScript: api.ugcTrust(playerId, on) Trusted creators' uploads skip the approval queue when the policy accepts "trusted". See also: set_trusted
docs.title: api.ugc_trust

docs.text: GDScript: api.ugc_ban(player_id: String, on := true, reason := "") -> void JavaScript: api.ugcBan(playerId, on, reason) Stops (or allows again) a player uploading creations; banning also hides their creations. See also: set_banned
docs.title: api.ugc_ban

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_permission(permission: String, description: String, roles := []) -> void JavaScript: api.registerPermission(permission: string, description: string, roles?: string[]): void Describes a permission a mod checks with player.has_permission, and which built-in roles get it by default (e.g. ["moderator"]; admins and owners have every permission anyway). api.register_permission("proving.prove", "May prove things", ["moderator"]) See also: merge , role
docs.title: api.register_permission

docs.text: GDScript: api.network_servers() -> Array JavaScript: api.networkServers(): { key: string; name: string; address: string; port: number; hop: boolean; inventory: boolean }[] The servers players can travel to from here (network.json): [{key, name, address, port, hop, inventory}].
docs.title: api.network_servers

docs.text: GDScript: api.set_arrival_point(id: String, position: Vector3) -> void JavaScript: api.setArrivalPoint(id, position) Names a spot where players arriving from other servers can appear (tickets name it as their arrival). See also: set_arrival
docs.title: api.set_arrival_point

docs.text: GDScript: api.raycast(origin: Vector3, direction: Vector3, max_distance := 5.0, options := {}) -> Dictionary JavaScript: api.raycast( origin: { x: number; y: number; z: number }, direction: { x: number; y: number; z: number }, maxDistance?: number, options?: { liquids?: boolean }, ): { hit: boolean; position?: { x: number; y: number; z: number }; normal?: { x: number; y: number; z: number }; block?: number } What a ray from origin in direction hits: {hit, position, normal, block} (position and normal are Vector3i; hit is false when it reaches max_distance or unloaded world). By default it sees what a player's crosshair sees, which deliberately looks straight through water - you aim at the riverbed, not the river. Pass {"liquids": true} when the liquid is the point: a fishing rod has to find the water's surface, and there is no other way to ask where that is. var look := api.look_direction(player) var hit := api.raycast(player.get_eye_position(), look, 6.0, {"liquids": true}) options.realm names the world to cast in; without it, the one a server starts with. var hit: Dictionary = api.raycast(player.get_eye_position(), api.look_direction(player), 6.0) See also: cast , qualified , raycast_lut_with_liquids , register_instance
docs.title: api.raycast

docs.text: GDScript: api.look_direction(player) -> Vector3 JavaScript: api.lookDirection(player) Where a player is looking, as a unit vector. The same direction the engine uses for their reach. See also: column
docs.title: api.look_direction

docs.text: GDScript: api.set_rejoin_handler(handler: Callable) -> void JavaScript: api.setRejoinHandler(handler) Where a player who has played here before comes back to: handler(player, saved_position) -> Vector3 . Return Vector3.INF to leave them where they logged out, which is what happens with no handler. A separate question from set_spawn_handler , and usually a different answer. A story might want a first-time arrival at the structure it placed, and everyone after that back in their own bed. A lobby server wants the opposite: everybody, every time, in the lobby. Answering both with one handler meant a mod could only have one of them. See also: decorate
docs.title: api.set_rejoin_handler

docs.text: GDScript: api.is_liquid(block: int) -> bool JavaScript: api.isLiquid(block: number): boolean Whether a block id is a liquid (water, lava, and anything a mod declares liquid: true ).
docs.title: api.is_liquid

docs.text: GDScript: api.area_cells(rule_name: String, ctx := {}) -> Array JavaScript: api.areaCells(ruleName, ctx) The cells a shape covers: "box" ({from, to}), "sphere" ({position, radius}), "vein" ({position, block, max}) or a shape a mod registered. max caps how many come back. var cells := api.area_cells("vein", {"position": at, "player": p, "max": 64}) Choosing the cells and changing them are separate on purpose: between the two is where a tool shows a preview, counts what it would cost, or asks whether the player really meant it. var cells: Array = api.area_cells("vein", {"position": at, "player": player, "max": 64}) See also: cells
docs.title: api.area_cells

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_area_rule(rule_name: String, chooser: Callable) -> void JavaScript: api.registerAreaRule(ruleName, chooser) Registers a way of choosing cells, for a tool the three built-in shapes do not describe - a line, a wall, everything touching one face. The callable is handed the context area_cells was called with and returns an Array of Vector3i. api.register_area_rule("column", func(ctx): var at: Vector3i = ctx.get("position", Vector3i.ZERO) var height: int = clampi(int(ctx.get("height", 4)), 1, 32) var out: Array = [] for dy in height: out.append(at + Vector3i(0, dy, 0)) return out) See also: register_rule
docs.title: api.register_area_rule

docs.text: GDScript: api.area_edit(player, cells: Array, options := {}) -> Dictionary JavaScript: api.areaEdit(player, cells, options) Changes every cell a player is allowed to change. block 0 (or absent) breaks instead of places. options: {block, drops (default true), realm}. Returns {changed, skipped, refused, reason}. This is not fill . Every cell goes through the plot check, the block events, the loot roll, tool wear and the player's edit budget, so a mod listening for block_broken hears this exactly as it hears a pickaxe, and a selection reaching into somebody's garden does the part outside it and reports the rest as skipped . fill is the admin door and asks none of that. var done: Dictionary = api.area_edit(player, cells, {"block": 0}) See also: apply
docs.title: api.area_edit

docs.text: GDScript: api.show_area(player, cells: Array, options := {}) -> void JavaScript: api.showArea(player, cells, options) Outlines a selection for one player, before they commit to it. seconds 0 holds it until it is cleared, which is what a tool with a live selection wants; an empty list takes it away. options: {color, seconds}. api.show_area(player, cells, {"seconds": 3.0}) See also: preview
docs.title: api.show_area

docs.text: GDScript: api.add_death_messages(key: String, lines: Array) -> void JavaScript: api.addDeathMessages(key, lines) More ways of saying that somebody died, so a mod’s own mobs get their own send-off rather than the engine’s general one. key is a cause ("lava", "fall", "magic") or the name of an entity; the first "%s" is the player and a second one is whatever did it. One is picked at random, never the same twice running, alongside the lines already there. api.add_death_messages("mymod:dragon", ["%s was toasted by %s", "%s argued with %s and lost"]) Keep them kind: say what happened, never what anyone is like. Children read these about themselves. See also: count , qualified , register_settings
docs.title: api.add_death_messages

docs.text: GDScript: api.register_settings(schema: Dictionary) -> void JavaScript: api.registerSettings(schema) Declares the settings a host may change without editing this mod, as {key: definition}. Each definition takes a type ("bool", "int", "float", "choice" or "text"), a label players see, an optional help line, a default , min / max / step for numbers and choices ([[value, label]]) for a choice. Call it while the mod loads; declaring the same key again updates its definition. api.register_settings({ "monster_rate": {"label": "How many monsters", "type": "float", "default": 1.0, "min": 0.0, "max": 3.0, "help": "Multiplies how often monsters appear."}, "difficulty": {"label": "Difficulty", "type": "choice", "default": "normal", "choices": [["easy", "Easy"], ["normal", "Normal"], ["hard", "Hard"]]}, }) The server owns the values, so all three ways in agree: mod_settings.json in the server's data folder, the /modsettings command, and the admin settings screen. They live in the world, so a world carries its own settings and a backup restores them. api.register_settings({ "monsters": {"label": "How many monsters", "type": "choice", "default": "normal", "choices": [["none", "None"], ["few", "A few"], ["normal", "Normal"], ["many", "Lots"]]}, "day_minutes": {"label": "Minutes in a day", "type": "int", "default": 20, "min": 2, "max": 120}, "zombies_burn": {"label": "Monsters burn by day", "type": "bool", "default": true}, }) See also: register
docs.title: api.register_settings

docs.text: GDScript: api.setting(key: String) JavaScript: api.setting(key) This mod's setting, as the host left it (its default until someone changes it). null if not declared. See also: get_value , is_game , on , show_title
docs.title: api.setting

docs.text: GDScript: api.is_game() -> bool JavaScript: api.isGame(): boolean Is this mod the game being played, or is it being used as a foundation by another one? A game mod is often somebody else's dependency: a story game builds on a sandbox one, so the sandbox's blocks, creatures and recipes are all wanted, but its title card and its welcome are not - the player is in the story. Guard anything that speaks for the whole game with this: api.on("player_join", func(ev): if api.is_game(): ev.player.show_title("Open Sandbox", "Build anything", 4.0)) The game is the first mod the server was asked to load that declares "kind": "game" ; a game loaded only because something else depends on it is not it. Add-ons (kind "addon") are never the game.
docs.title: api.is_game

docs.text: GDScript: api.game_id() -> String JavaScript: api.gameId() The id of the game being played, whichever mod this is. Useful for an add-on that wants to behave differently depending on the game it has been added to.
docs.title: api.game_id

docs.text: GDScript: api.settings() -> Dictionary JavaScript: api.settings() Every setting of this mod as {key: value}, for passing to something that wants a config dictionary. See also: get_block_data , list , merge
docs.title: api.settings

docs.text: GDScript: api.set_setting(key: String, value) -> String JavaScript: api.setSetting(key, value) Changes one of this mod's settings from code (the same path the admin screen uses, so handlers of settings_changed run). Returns "" or why it was refused. See also: set_value
docs.title: api.set_setting

docs.text: GDScript: api.static qualified(ref: String, owner: String) -> String JavaScript: api.qualified(ref, owner) The same rule, for the capabilities that hold names a mod wrote inside a definition - a shop's ledger, a character's shop - and so must qualify them against that mod rather than against whoever happens to be asking later. Public because three things need it and a private function two systems copy is a fact about the code that ought to be visible in the code.
docs.title: api.qualified

docs.text: Guidebook and tutorials Part of the Mod API reference . Mod API 1.0.0 · game 0.42.0 api.register_guide_chapter GDScript: api.register_guide_chapter(chapter_name: String, def := {}) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerGuideChapter(chapterName, def) A guidebook chapter: {title, icon (item name), order, description}. Names without ":" are this mod's. api.register_guide_chapter("proving", {"title": "The Proving Ground", "order": 1}) See also: add_chapter , item , qualified api.register_guide_page GDScript: api.register_guide_page(page_name: String, def: Dictionary) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerGuidePage(pageName, def) A guidebook page (see engine/shared/guide_registry.gd): {chapter, title, icon, order, unlock: {item (a name or a list of names, any of which opens it) | recipe | entity | flag | page}, hint, keywords, blocks: [{type: text | heading | items | recipe | entity | image | tip | link | keys, ...}]}. Item, entity, page and flag names without ":" are this mod's; image blocks take a texture path in this mod. api.register_guide_page("what", {"chapter": "proving", "title": "What this is", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "A mod that exists to be tested."}]}) See also: add_page , qualified , register_asset api.open_guide GDScript: api.open_guide(player, page := "") -> void JavaScript: api.openGuide(player, page) Opens the guidebook for a player at a page ("" = where they left off). See also: open , qualified api.set_guide_flag GDScript: api.set_guide_flag(player, flag: String, on := true) -> void JavaScript: api.setGuideFlag(player, flag, on) Guide flags unlock pages with unlock: {flag} (names without ":" are this mod's). Saved per player. See also: qualified , set_flag api.has_guide_flag GDScript: api.has_guide_flag(player, flag: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.hasGuideFlag(player, flag) Whether a player has a guide flag (see set_guide_flag). See also: has_flag , qualified api.unlock_guide_page GDScript: api.unlock_guide_page(player, page: String, notify := true) -> bool JavaScript: api.unlockGuidePage(player, page, notify) Unlocks a guide page for a player whatever its condition. Returns true if it was locked. See also: qualified , unlock api.is_guide_page_unlocked GDScript: api.is_guide_page_unlocked(player, page: String) -> bool JavaScript: api.isGuidePageUnlocked(player, page) Whether a guide page is open to a player. See also: is_unlocked , qualified api.register_tutorial GDScript: api.register_tutorial(tutorial_name: String, def: Dictionary) -> bool JavaScript: api.registerTutorial(tutorialName, def) A tutorial: guided goals completed by real actions (see engine/server/tutorials.gd for goal types): {title, description, order, auto_start, reward: [[item, count]], steps: [{title, text, icon, goal: {type, target, count, ...}, hint: {block | entity | position} or false, page, reward}]}.
